minutes.headline: PACC heard a proposal to replace studio cameras with a standardized 4K system; no vote on it, minutes approved with September 11 date.
minutes.summary: The committee corrected the next meeting date to September 11 and approved the minutes. The manager reported on new affiliates, a new videographer hire, FY23 close-out and ideas for live programming. Most of the meeting was a discussion of replacing the studio cameras and switcher with a 4K ecosystem, plus youth outreach and sponsorship wording awaiting the town lawyer.

budget_items.what_was_said: The manager must ask the Personnel committee for a higher-than-step-one entry rate for a new hire with extensive experience, then Selectmen approval is needed.
The manager has worked on numbers with Eric. There was a question whether spending follows normal purchasing and is outside the town-meeting-set budget; he will check with accounting.
FY23 was closed out after late interest postings and the ending balance was stated.
Interest earned in May and June was noted, with two payments in May unexplained.
Replacing current cameras with upgraded models was floated at a per-camera cost, with Blackmagic Studio Camera 4K Pro as the example.
PTZ systems were described as very expensive.
The current TriCaster is about five years old and no longer supported; a replacement switcher would do more.
Each Blackmagic hardware item reportedly includes a permanent Resolve Studio license, versus a monthly Adobe cost.
Idea of accepting small gift certificates or donations as contest rewards, pending the town lawyer's reading of the contract.
A member complained that the quarterly report on invested funds was nearly useless.

what_happened.line: The committee discussed replacing the studio cameras and the TriCaster switcher with a standardized 4K system; no vote was taken, and any change would be tested for about two months first.
The next meeting date was corrected to September 11, 2023 in the minutes and agenda, and the minutes were approved with that change, though the vote result was not audible in the captions.
The manager reported on a new videographer hire, which needs a Personnel committee request for an above-step-one starting rate and then Selectmen approval.
FY23 was closed out after late interest postings, and two May payments were noted as unexplained.
Sponsorship wording, including small gift certificates as contest rewards, awaits the town lawyer's reading of the contract.

why_it_matters: Replacing the studio cameras and switcher would be a capital purchase for the town's public access cable operation, and no cost has been voted or put in a budget yet.
The hire's starting rate and the open question of whether this spending follows normal purchasing both bear on how the cable account is spent outside the budget set at town meeting.
watch_next: The next PACC meeting on September 11, 2023, and whether the manager reports back on the equipment testing and on accounting's answer about purchasing rules.
The town lawyer's reply on sponsorship and gift-certificate wording.
